title: Hallmark Signatures of Electronic Pairing in Two-Photon Two-Electron Coincidence Angle-Resolved Photoemission Spectroscopy
authors: Janez Bonca, Alberto Nocera, Andrea Damascelli, Mona Berciu
abstract: Understanding strongly correlated quantum materials remains a central challenge in condensed matter physics and materials science. While angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) has become an indispensable probe of single-quasiparticle excitations, it accesses electronic correlations only indirectly. Here we show that unlike one-photon in, two-electrons out coincidence ARPES ($γ\!\rightarrow\!2e$ 2eARPES), the two-photon in, two-electron out $2γ\!\rightarrow\!2e$ 2eARPES provides a direct and unambiguous probe of electronic pairing. We establish this on general theoretical grounds and substantiate it through large-scale numerical simulations of strongly correlated models with both paired and unpaired ground states. The key result is a model-independent separation in the $(ω_1,ω_2)$ plane of the two photoelectrons' energies, between signal from electrons emitted from the \emph{same} pair and signal from electrons emitted from \emph{different} pairs; this follows from energy conservation alone and is independent of any material-specific assumptions. Our findings demonstrate that $2γ\!\rightarrow\!2e$ 2eARPES can identify pairing and extract the pair binding energy as well as the energy of the 'glue' boson without any sophisticated data analysis or complementary measurements.
summary: The paper introduces two-photon two-electron coincidence ARPES ($2\gamma 	o 2e$ $2e$ARPES) as a superior technique for studying electronic pairing in correlated materials. Theoretically, it shows that this method yields an unambiguous energy separation between photoemission signals originating from electrons within the same pair versus those from different pairs. This allows for model-independent identification of superconducting signatures directly from the coincidence spectrum.
main_problem: To develop a method that provides a direct and unambiguous probe of electronic pairing in strongly correlated quantum materials, overcoming limitations of standard ARPES.
main_result: Two-photon two-electron coincidence ARPES ($2\gamma 	o 2e$ $2e$ARPES) offers a model-independent separation in the photoemission energy plane between signals from electrons originating from the same pair and those from different pairs, allowing direct measurement of pairing signatures.
method: Theoretical derivation of coincident photoelectron intensity formulas and comparison of spectral weight regions in the $(\omega_1, \omega_2)$ energy plane for paired versus unpaired ground states.
model_or_system: The study applies general theoretical grounds to strongly correlated electron systems, modeled using frameworks like the Hubbard model or Hubbard-Holstein model. The analysis focuses on distinguishing between paired and unpaired electronic ground states.
key_observables: Coincidence photoelectron intensity $D(\omega_1, \omega_2)$ in the $(\omega_1, \omega_2)$ energy plane; specific energy bounds related to pair binding energy ($\Delta$) and boson energy ($\Omega$).
important_parameters: Pairing gap ($\Delta$), pair binding energy, chemical potential ($\mu$), and the photon/boson energies ($\omega_{ph}, \Omega$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the sudden approximation when photoelectrons depart; results are derived at zero temperature but expected to apply to preformed pair liquids.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the spectral weight regions in the $(\omega_1, \omega_2)$ plane for both quasiparticle liquid and paired states, showing distinct boundaries separating type-(i) (different pairs) and type-(ii) (same pair) emission signals.
paper_structure: The paper establishes general theoretical grounds by deriving intensity formulas, analyzes the spectral separation in the $(\omega_1, \omega_2)$ plane for both paired and unpaired systems using numerical simulations of correlated models, and contrasts this method with one-photon setups.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful spectroscopic diagnostic tool applicable to strongly correlated materials, offering a way to probe pairing mechanisms directly without relying on complex material-specific assumptions or complementary measurements.

figures.caption: Figure 1. Shaded regions indicate where 2γ →2e 2eARPES spec- tral weight can appear in the (ω1, ω2) plane of the photoelectrons’ energies, for (a) a quasiparticle liquid and (b) a liquid of pairs with binding energy ∆; µ is the chemical potential. In (b), the orange re- gions labeled ‘(ii)’ are accessible only when both electrons originate from the same pair, while the blue region admits contributions from electrons ejected from different pairs, labeled ‘(i)’. The significance of the solid and dashed lines is explained in the text.

Figure 2. Momentum-integrated 2eARPES weight D(ω1, ω2) for the pure Hubbard model (λ = 0). Left column: VED results for Ne = 2, N = 90. Right column: DMRG results for Ne = 12, N = 48 (n = 0.25). In all panels tel = 1, U = −3, −2, +2 (top to bottom), and η = 0.05. Lines as in Fig. 1.

Figure 3. Momentum-integrated 2eARPES weight D(ω1, ω2) for the pure Holstein model (U = 0, λ = 1.0, Ω= 1.0, tph = 0). (a) VED results for Ne = 2, N = 34 (n →0). (b)–(d) DMRG results for N = 48 and Ne = 4, 8, 12, respectively. Lines as in Fig. 1, with µ and ∆ extracted from DMRG.

Figure 4. Counterparts to Fig. 1 for the γ →2e setup. (a) Unpaired case: the dotted orange line marks the global energy maximum for γ →2e processes. (b) Paired case: the dotted orange (dashed white) line marks the global maximum for type-(ii) [type-(i)] γ →2e pro- cesses. Blue shaded regions show where conventional γ →e ARPES weight is expected; unlike for the 2γ →2e setup, here the 2eARPES signal is not energetically separated from this background.
